caption:
When you die, your deeds stop. Except three.

"When a man dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: a charity that keeps going, knowledge that people benefit from, or a righteous child who prays for him." (Sahih Muslim 1631)

A well. A Quran in a masjid. Teaching someone Al-Fatiha. A child saying "O Allah, forgive my parents."

And "whoever guides to good gets the same reward as the one who does it" (Muslim 1893, Tirmidhi 2671). Send someone to pray, and you pray with them. Forever.

caption:
Is it a sin to struggle with desire?

Yusuf (AS) won this fight, but not the way you'd think. She locked every door and said “come”. He didn't stand there trying to be strong. He said “Ma'adhallah, I seek refuge in Allah” and ran for the door (Quran 12:23–25).

“Thus We turned evil and immorality away from him. He was one of Our chosen servants.” (12:24)

The Prophet ﷺ said a man called by a woman of beauty and status who says “I fear Allah” will be shaded by Allah on the Day there is no shade but His (Bukhari 660, Muslim 1031).

Feeling the pull isn't the sin. Tonight: get up, leave the room, put the phone down. Comment APP and I'll DM you the app that pauses your apps at every adhan.

caption:
Ayat al-Kursi has a hidden centre.

The Prophet ﷺ called it the greatest verse in the Quran (Sahih Muslim 810). Split it at its pauses and you get 9 sentences that mirror each other: His names ↔ His names, no drowsiness ↔ never tired, the heavens and earth ↔ His Kursi over them, by His permission ↔ as He wills. And one sentence has no twin, right in the middle: “He knows what is before them and what is behind them.”

Who builds a verse like this?

Recite it after every prayer: “nothing will stand between him and Jannah except death” (an-Nasa'i al-Kubra 9928, sahih per al-Albani). Comment APP and I'll DM you the app that pauses your apps at every adhan, so you never miss the prayers it comes after.
